text:
A: Hi. Can you hear me?
B: Yeah. Hiya.
A: I'm Ioana.
B: Courtney.
A: Where are you?
B: Sunderland. You?
A: North West London. Burnt Oak.
B: Right.
A: Yeah.
B: Erm... what do you do, then?
A: Lettings admin. Estate agent's in Edgware.
B: No way. That's what I do. Well, part-time. Lettings and property management, in town.
A: Seriously? Okay. What are you on, phones?
B: Phones, booking viewings, chasing tenants for paperwork. And I scan everything into this system nobody else in the office understands. Like, I set the folders up, and now if I'm off nobody can find anything, so they just ring me. On my day off. To ask where a gas certificate is.
A: [laughs] That's me. Exactly that. I'm the one who knows where everything is, and they ring me on a Saturday.
B: Do the negotiators promise tenants stuff and then just leave it?
A: All the time. "Oh, yeah, the landlord will definitely sort the boiler." He won't. He's never sorted anything. Then the tenant rings me and I'm the one getting shouted at, and the negotiator's out doing a viewing in his Mini.
B: Ours is called Craig. He's always out doing a viewing.
A: There's always a Craig.
B: [laughs] Yeah.
A: Do you want to stay in it? Lettings?
B: Not really. It pays for stuff. I draw, that's what I actually want to do, illustration. But I'm realistic, like. I'll be scanning tenancy agreements for a bit.
A: I'm doing an accounting course, AAT. So I can get into property accounts. Fewer phone calls.
B: Fewer phone calls sounds amazing, ngl.
A: That's honestly the main reason.
B: Yeah.
A: What kind of drawing?
B: Ink, mostly. Kind of creepy stuff, people say. Moths and that. I read a lot of horror, so it sort of comes from there.
A: I read crime. Thrillers, on the bus. Not horror, though, I can't sleep after.
B: I'm the opposite, I can't sleep anyway, so I just end up on Wikipedia at two in the morning reading about unsolved stuff. Like, the Dyatlov Pass thing, have you heard of that? These hikers in Russia in the fifties who cut their way out of their tent from the inside and ran off into the snow with no shoes on, and there's about twenty theories, and I've read all of them, and none of them really work. I think that's why I like it, it doesn't finish properly.
A: No, see, that would do my head in. I want to know who did it. That's why I like detective stuff, it gets solved.
B: Fair. Real life doesn't, though.
A: That's why I like the books.
B: [laughs] Okay, that's actually a good point.
A: Someone just told me about a podcast, two women drinking wine and talking about murders. I said I'd try it.
B: Are you going to?
A: Probably not.
B: Yeah, I wouldn't.
